"Whenever women see another woman with a beautiful form, adorned with gold, silver, precious gems, and various pearls, and experience great pleasure in her body, they give rise to a mind of attachment upon seeing her. They are unable to observe this body as it truly is—as a mere heap of excrement, foul, impure, and unclean—which is only temporarily embellished by colors and various perfumes. These deceive the eyes of the ignorant, causing them to give rise to defilement and attachment, and thus, through the arising of various afflictions, they receive a female body."
Furthermore, Siṃha!

By their very nature, women are prone to much stinginess and envy; what they say at one time differs from what they think at another, and what they say in your presence differs from what they say in private. For the sake of worldly gratification, there are some women who do not seek the True Dharma, being obscured by anger and shrouded by sloth, delighting instead in idle chatter. For these reasons, they are unable to receive and uphold this sutra.

Furthermore, because their minds are predominantly defiled throughout day and night and lack the mind of renunciation, they possess such afflicted states of mind that they constantly receive female bodies and are unable to bring them to an end.
Therefore, Siṃha!
If a woman wishes not to give rise to afflictions and does not wish to receive a female body, she should accept, uphold, read, and recite this sutra, and explain it for others.
"Why is this? Because this sutra is able to eliminate all the afflictions of women.
Siṃha again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If there is a woman who, without being free from her female body, upholds this sutra, recites it, and masters its meaning, will she continue to receive a female body?”
The Buddha told Siṃha:

"If there is a woman who, though not yet liberated from her female body, upholds this sutra, reciting and mastering it, you should know that this present body shall be her very last. This applies except for those who manifest a female body through their supernormal powers."
"Siṃha! It is as if, for example, someone were to throw himself into a great mass of fire and say:
'Do not burn my body; do not burn my skin and complexion.'"
"What do you think?
Would what this person says accord with your wishes?
Siṃha replied to the Buddha:
"No, World-Honored One. Why is this so? Because..."
"The nature of fire destroys a person's physical form and appearance.
The Buddha told Siṃha:
"This sutra is likewise; it burns away all afflictions until nothing remains."
Therefore, Siṃha!

If there is a woman who wishes not to receive a female body, who wishes to quickly attain all Buddha-dharmas, who wishes to behold immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, who wishes to obtain unimpeded eloquence, and who wishes to universally encompass all sentient beings with a heart of loving-kindness, she should accept, uphold, read, recite, master, and explain this sutra for others.
At that time, Siṃha and the five hundred maidens said to the Buddha,
“World-Honored One!
We have upheld this sutra since our time under Dīpaṃkara Buddha!”
"In this manner, it has been passed down through successive generations until the present day.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
“Is this Lion Girl not yet finished with her female form?
The Buddha said to Ānanda, “What do you think? Do you consider Siṃhā to be a woman?”
Ānanda replied to the Buddha,
“So it is, World-Honored One!
The Buddha said to Ānanda:
"Do not speak such words. Why is this?
This Lion and the five hundred maidens have manifested in female bodies through their supernormal powers (*ṛddhi*) out of compassion and for the benefit of women in future ages."
Why is this? Because no man may enter the houses of others at will.
Therefore, Ānanda!

The maiden Siṃhacandrā, through her supernormal powers, manifested the appearance of a female body; yet this woman possessed neither the qualities of a woman, nor the qualities of a man, nor the qualities of one who is neither male nor female.
Why is this? Because the female nature, the male nature, and the nature of neither male nor female are unattainable. Ānanda!
This Lion, within this Dharma, did not apprehend any dharma; she accomplished the patience of dharmas (dharmakṣānti) and attained great illumination.
Therefore, Ānanda, all women should follow her example and train as the maiden Siṃhā has done, upholding this sūtra, reading and reciting it until it is mastered, and explaining it for others.

At that time, there were five thousand bhikṣuṇīs in the assembly who rose from their seats, bared their right shoulders, placed their right knees on the ground, and with single-minded devotion joined their palms and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"From this day forward, I shall receive, uphold, read, recite, master, and explain this sutra for others.
Why is this? Because I do not wish or desire to undergo a female body again."
"Having undertaken the upholding of this sutra, if one has not ultimately read, recited, and mastered it, one shall never sit, lie down, nor sleep.
The Buddha addressed the bhikṣuṇīs:
"Excellent, excellent!"
They spoke these words:
"We shall adorn ourselves with the great adornment and exert ourselves with great diligence. Why is this?"

Since you do not delight in female bodies but joyfully seek the Buddha-dharma, you should therefore redouble your diligence, firmly resolve to uphold, receive, read, and recite this sutra, and master it thoroughly so as to explain it for others. You should know that this female body you have received is your very last.

At that time, the bhikṣuṇīs, hearing what the Buddha had spoken, were filled with joy and leaped for gladness. Each of them removed the *uttarāsaṅga* they were wearing and scattered it over the Buddha, speaking these verses:
“The Buddha speaks no double words; We shall certainly attain the male body.
Since you have declared that we shall become Buddhas, Our aspirations are fulfilled.”

At that time, there were five thousand laywomen in the assembly who, having heard these verses from the bhikṣuṇīs, immediately rose from their seats, bared their right shoulders, placed their right knees on the ground, and with palms joined in single-minded devotion, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We who now uphold this sutra, read it, recite it with mastery, and explain it to others—why is this?

It is because we now wish to distance ourselves from the lack of self-mastery, where one must watch the countenances of others like a maidservant or concubine. Although a woman’s body may be born into a royal family and raised there, she is given away in marriage to another king and gains no autonomy; for the duration of her life, she serves her husband, and having been pregnant for ten months, she undergoes manifold sufferings. For these reasons, from this day forward we shall apply ourselves with diligent effort to uphold this sutra and explain it to others.

Observing the practice of eating but one meal a day and upholding the precepts, she shall not let her side touch the ground; even at the cost of her life, she vows never to join hands with or draw near to her husband, but must instead receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the housewives, saying:
"Excellent, excellent!
O virtuous women, you have spoken these words most skillfully."

From this day forward, you shall no longer be subject to others; you shall always attain sovereignty, need not look to the countenances of others, and shall be free from the suffering of pregnancy. You shall no longer dwell in a womb, but be born in the Buddha-worlds where there is no lust and no women.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
As for the places where these sisters have been born, what are the names of those worlds and what are the titles of the Buddhas there?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"There is a world named Array of Many Jewel Flowers; the Buddha there is named Light of the Emanated King of All Jewel Maṇis, a Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, who currently dwells and teaches the Dharma. These women shall be reborn in that land."
“Because these laywomen’s wives have received and upheld this sutra, they shall be able to see that Buddha.

At that time, having heard this teaching, all the laywomen’s wives were filled with joy; their exultation was immeasurable. They immediately untied ten thousand strings of pearl necklaces from their necks and scattered them over the Buddha. Then, before the Buddha, they spoke in verse:
“We have obtained a great benefit, Having attained liberation from the female body;”
The Buddha has no double-tongued speech; all that he says is true and real.
He has forever cast off such a body, the lowly and base appearance of a woman;
it merely deceives those without wisdom, who cannot know according to reality.
Furthermore, one will no longer be like a maidservant or concubine, dependent on others and lacking self-mastery;
nor will one again undergo the ten months of pregnancy and its manifold sufferings.
One shall never again experience the various evils of dwelling within a womb.
"Having attained the wisdom that transcends the womb, this wisdom is unsurpassed.

When the wives of the householders had spoken these verses, they prostrated themselves with their heads at the Buddha’s feet, circumambulated him three times to the right, and then sat down together not far from the Buddha. With single-minded attention, they gazed upon the Buddha, their eyes never blinking for a moment.
At that time, Śakra Devānām-indra scattered divine kausumbha flowers over the Buddha and spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!
I shall receive, uphold, read, recite, master, and explain this sutra for the sake of others."
The Buddha told Śakra Devānām Indra:
“Kauśika! If you act in this way, you shall never again have to wage war against the asuras.”

At that time, the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī, wishing to cause the roots of goodness possessed by hundreds of thousands of sentient beings to become even more radiant and pure, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
"In the past, the Tathāgata heard this sūtra from me and thereby gave rise to the bodhicitta.

The Buddha told Mañjuśrī, "For this reason, among an assembly of hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of bodhisattvas, you are the most brilliantly illuminating; you awaken sentient beings throughout the worlds of the ten directions, like the light of the sun."
Immediately, the great earth shook, and the heavens rained down various flowers that gathered around the World-Honored One Buddha until they reached his knees.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!”
“For what cause and condition does the great earth tremble, and why are these various celestial flowers scattered, piling up to the knees?
The Buddha told Ānanda:

“Now hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of devas, having heard these words spoken by Mañjuśrī, have leaped for joy and scattered various celestial flowers, all exclaiming these words:”
"We shall receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra and explain it to others. Just as the Dharma Prince Mañjuśrī has so eloquently spoken these words, we too shall follow and learn from them;
just as Mañjuśrī illuminates the world, we too shall likewise illuminate it."

When these words were spoken, they all attained the recollection of this sutra as if it were present before them; therefore, their hearts gave rise to immeasurable joy and exultation, and they further heard that they had received this sutra from me through Mañjuśrī.
"Ānanda! For this reason, the great earth trembles and the heavens rain down manifold flowers.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
This sutra accomplishes all great merits; this sutra accomplishes unprecedented merits. It is not for sentient beings who have accomplished only meager roots of goodness to hear this sutra.”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“So it is, so it is! It is just as you have said.”

If good sons or good daughters, having made offerings to immeasurable hundreds of thousands of Buddhas, hear this sutra; and having heard it, believe, understand, accept, uphold, read, recite, and explain it to others.

Ānanda! You should know that this son of good family is like a stūpa among gods and humans. In whichever direction a person dwells who upholds, maintains, reads, or recites this sutra, in that very place there shall be a person of bright and upright Dharma.
Furthermore, Ānanda!

If there are those who receive, uphold, read, recite, and master this sutra, and explain it for others, or even transcribe it into volumes and make offerings to it, you should know that such persons have escaped all evil destinies; they have already been able to subdue the evil Māra Pāpīyān; they have established the banner of the Dharma and are able to practice the gift of Dharma; they have lit the great Dharma-torch to shatter the darkness of ignorance; they have blown the great Dharma-conch to advance toward the site of enlightenment (bodhimaṇḍa); they have struck the great Dharma-drum to open the gate of ambrosia and let fall the great Dharma-rain, thereby satisfying all who joyfully seek the Dharma.

He opens the treasuries of all dharmas gathered by the Buddhas and brings forth the great wealth of the Dharma; he knows that all dharmas are far removed from all conceptualizations—namely, the conceptualizations of form, sensation, perception, formations, and consciousness; the conceptualizations of eye, ear, nose, tongue, body, and mind; the conceptualizations of forms, sounds, odors, tastes, tangibles, and phenomena; he is far removed from all conceptualizations of dharmas, even including the conceptualizations of Buddha, Dharma, and Sangha.

Ānanda! If there are those who hear this sutra from me, receive, uphold, read, and recite it, you should know that such persons are my children, born from the Buddha’s own mouth and born from the Dharma-body.
Therefore, Ānanda!

If there are sentient beings who wish to partake of the Tathāgata’s food, who wish to sit at the site of enlightenment, and who wish to preach the True Dharma just as I do now, they should receive, uphold, read, recite, and master this sutra, and explain it for others; furthermore, they should copy its scrolls, receive, uphold, and make offerings to them.
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

Those in future ages who receive, uphold, read, recite, and master this sutra, and who explain it for others, or even transcribe its scrolls and make offerings to them—are they all those who today receive, uphold, read, and recite this sutra?”
The Buddha told Ānanda: "So it is, so it is! Why is this? Because..."

I have never seen anyone else in all the worlds—whether among devas, humans, māras, brahmās, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, humans, or non-humans—who could preach this sutra in a future age and cause others to hear it; such a thing is impossible.
Ānanda! One who is able to accumulate the wealth of the Dharma today will be able to enjoy it at will in future lives.

It is like a householder or a householder’s son whose family is immensely wealthy and possesses abundant treasures—gold, silver, lapis lazuli, pearls, mani-jewels, conch shells, jade, and granaries overflowing with grain; with such a multitude of servants, slaves, elephants, horses, oxen, and sheep, if he were to travel to another region for pleasure and sightseeing, would that person, upon returning later, still be able to enjoy his wealth?
Ānanda said to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
It is because they have the freedom to enjoy them as their own wealth.”
“Thus it is, Ānanda!
Those who have heard this sutra in my presence shall likewise hear it in future ages; they shall receive, uphold, read, and recite such a scripture, and shall offer worship just as they do today.”

Ānanda! With my Buddha-eye, I see those who have faith and understanding, who receive and uphold this sutra, read and recite it with mastery, explain it to others, and even transcribe its volumes as they do now, Ānanda!
"And yet, those who make offerings shall likewise see those who revile and do not believe or accept [the teaching].
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"If there are sentient beings who do not believe or understand this sutra and instead slander it, where will that person's karmic retribution lead them to be born?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Stop! Do not ask."
"There is no need to ask.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"I only pray that you will explain this, so that those sentient beings who do not yet believe in this Dharma may give rise to faith and joy.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"The place where such a person’s karmic retribution arises is equal to that of the five deeds of immediate retribution."
Ānanda! What do you think?
Suppose there were a person who, within a single day, were to sever the life-faculties of all sentient beings in a trichiliocosm; what would be the retribution for the place of birth of that person?
Ānanda said to the Buddha:
“It is most evil,
World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“That person’s retribution for their sin shall also be equal to theirs. Ānanda!”
What do you think?

Suppose there were someone who destroyed or burned the stūpas and temples erected after the parinirvāṇa of as many Buddhas as there are grains of sand in the Ganges River; would the demerit they incur be great?
Ānanda said to the Buddha,
“It is very much so,
World-Honored One!”
"The eyes should not look, and the ears should not hear.
The Buddha said to Ānanda:
"What kind of retribution for sin will that person receive in their place of birth?"
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
It is most evil and most grave.”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“That person’s retribution for their sin shall also be equal to theirs. Ānanda!”
What do you think?
Suppose there were a person who disrupts and corrupts the true Dharma of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present;
what would their transgression be?
Ānanda said to the Buddha:
“It is very heavy,
World-Honored One!”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"That person's retribution for their sin shall be equal to theirs.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If there are those who disparage and slander this sutra, causing sentient beings to distance themselves from it,
what would their transgression be?”
The Buddha said to Ānanda:
“What do you think?
Suppose all sentient beings in the trichiliocosm were to practice the ten wholesome paths and seek anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi, and someone were to destroy their eyes.”
"Would their transgression be great?
Ānanda replied to the Buddha,
"It would be very great."
“World-Honored One!
For hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of kalpas, one shall undergo various sufferings within the hells.
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"I now tell you: if there are sentient beings who slander this sutra, or even cause a single person to distance themselves from it, you should know that their transgression is equal to those [who have committed the aforementioned offenses]."
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If there should be a bodhisattva who seeks anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi and, although harboring doubts regarding this sutra, does not slander it.”
"What is their transgression?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"If one gives rise to a doubting mind, they oppose all Buddhas and commit an offense; for one hundred million kalpas, they shall remain far removed from Bodhi."
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!

If there are sentient beings who slander this sutra and cause many other sentient beings to distance themselves from it, how great will be the body they receive as retribution for their transgression?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Stop! There is no need to ask whether this body of transgression is large or small."
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We pray that you will explain this, so that the fourfold assembly and sentient beings of future generations may feel shame and dread.”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“That person’s body of sin shall be ten thousand yojanas in length, and they will undergo immeasurable suffering.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“If that person was unable to guard their speech, what will be the size of the retribution they receive for their tongue?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“The tongue of that sinner shall be one thousand yojanas in length and breadth; five hundred iron plows, blazing with fierce flames, shall till that tongue.”
"Furthermore, five hundred iron balls, blazing with fierce flames, shall rain down upon his tongue because he failed to guard his speech in previous lives.

At that time, the fourfold assembly was struck with terror; their body hair stood on end, and they wept with tears streaming down as they threw themselves to the ground. With one voice, they spoke these words:
"World-Honored One!
We now confess and repent on behalf of those sons and daughters of noble family, wishing that they may remain far removed from such a body of sin and not undergo these manifold sufferings.
Within the assembly, there were others who wept and shed tears, speaking thus:
“World-Honored One!

Whether in this life, or in our previous hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of nayutas of lives, if we have ever given rise to doubt and thereby created the causes and conditions for these manifold sufferings, we now, before the Tathāgata, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, and before the remaining hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of immeasurable Buddhas, World-Honored Ones, openly confess and repent.”

May all the Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, behold and know us with their Buddha-eyes. Whatever karmic offenses we now possess, we fully disclose them and dare not conceal them. We are foolish and small-minded, ignorant, lacking in awakening, and devoid of skillful means; we only pray that the Buddhas, out of compassion, will accept our repentance.
The Buddha addressed the sons of good family:
“Excellent, excellent!
That you now, before me, do not conceal your offenses but openly confess and repent, brings increase to my Dharma.”
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Will all those in this assembly who have now conceived doubts undergo such suffering in hell?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"Those in this assembly who have now conceived doubts will have very little sin remaining because they have repented.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“How much suffering will that person undergo?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“When that person is about to die, they will experience immeasurable suffering within each and every pore of their body, yet it will not last long.”
Why is this? Because they have confessed their transgressions before me and before other immeasurable and boundless Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones. Ānanda!

Therefore, sons and daughters of good family who do not wish to receive such a body of transgression, such a tongue of transgression, and such manifold sufferings, should have faith and understanding in this sutra and harbor no doubts.

Ānanda! If there are good men or good women who do not wish to abandon the Buddha, the Dharma, or the Saṅgha of bhikṣus; who do not wish to abandon the true Dharma of the Buddhas of the past, future, and present—they should receive, uphold, read, recite, master, and explain this sūtra to others, and they should copy it into volumes and make offerings to them.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
The Tathāgata now speaks the *Avaivartika-cakra-sūtra*; for what reason do you say, ‘If one does not abandon the Saṃgha’?”
“Which monk does he not abandon?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“The so-called ‘Saṃgha’ refers to those who have attained non-retrogression; those who have gathered for the sake of the Dharma of non-retrogression are also called the Saṃgha.”
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying,
“Does a bodhisattva who regresses not belong within the number of the Saṃgha?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"If there are those who have deeply resolved for bodhicitta but do not perceive this mind, they shall all enter the assembly of non-retrogressive monks.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"How rare, World-Honored One! All Buddhas have accomplished the power of great skillful means; by means of such skillful means, they preach the Dharma in this way."
At that time, Śakra-devānām-indra scattered heavenly māndārava flowers over the Buddha and addressed him, saying:
“World-Honored One!
May all sentient beings achieve such skillful means as these.”
The Buddha told Śakra-devānām-indra:
“Kauśika! If there are those who have faith and understanding in this sutra, they shall all achieve such skillful means in expounding all dharmas as I do now, being exactly equal and no different.”
At that time, hundreds of thousands of devas scattered celestial māndārava flowers over the Buddha and spoke these words:
"May all sentient beings attain this sutra."
At that time, Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
We pray that the Tathāgata, out of compassion for future sentient beings, will protect this sutra.”
At that time, the Buddha told Ānanda:
"If good men or good women should hear this sutra while in the great ocean, those good men and good women shall all indeed hear it."
"Why is this? Because it has already been protected by the Tathāgatas of former Buddhas.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Although the Buddhas and Tathāgatas of the past protected this sutra, the Tathāgata now, out of compassion for sentient beings, should likewise protect it.

At that moment, the great earth shook in six ways, and immediately before the Buddha, Jambūnada-gold-colored celestial flowers appeared spontaneously. These flowers had hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of petals and emitted a great radiance that shone throughout the Buddha-worlds of the Ganges-sand in the ten directions.

At that time, the fourfold assembly all beheld the Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, in worlds as numerous as the sands of the Ganges throughout the ten directions; before each of these Buddhas, there also appeared spontaneously golden celestial flowers from the Jambūnada River with hundreds of thousands of myriads of koṭis of petals, emitting great radiance that shone everywhere throughout the ten directions.
At that time, Śakra-devānām-indra immediately transformed himself into the form of a layman, took various kinds of flowers, and spoke thus to the fourfold assembly:
"O virtuous ones!
"Now you may scatter these flowers over the Tathāgata, and also use them as an offering to this Dharma of the sutra.
At that time, the fourfold assembly took the flowers and scattered them over the Tathāgata.
By the spiritual power of the Buddha, the flowers scattered there transformed into flower canopies above each of the Buddhas.
At that time, the fourfold assembly addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
For what reason does the great earth tremble?

This great lotus has appeared spontaneously before all the Buddhas; likewise, it appears in as many Buddha-worlds as there are sands in the Ganges in the eastern direction, and so too in the southern, western, and northern directions, the four intermediate points, and the zenith and nadir, throughout as many Buddha-worlds as there are sands in the Ganges.
The Buddha addressed the fourfold assembly:
"If these signs appear beforehand, you should know that the Buddhas have already protected this sutra.
At that time, Ānanda said to the Buddha:
“World-Honored One!
Has the Tathāgata now already protected this sutra?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"So it is, so it is! I have already guarded it.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“Does only the Buddha, the World-Honored One, protect this sutra, or do the Buddhas of other worlds also protect it?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“The Buddhas, the World-Honored Ones, as numerous as the sands of the Ganges in the ten directions, also protect this sutra.”
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One,
what should this sutra be named?”
"How should it be received and upheld?
The Buddha told Ānanda:

"This sutra is named 'Non-attachment to All Fruits,' and it is also named 'Distancing from All Fruits. It is also named 'Expounding the Profound Meaning of Firm Faith, Firm Dharma, the Eight Persons, Srotāpanna, Sakṛdāgāmin, Anāgāmin, Arhat, Śrāvaka, and Pratyekabuddha. It is also named 'Subduing and Expelling Māras,' and it is also named 'Corresponding with the Six Pāramitās.'"

Why is this? If good sons or good daughters believe and understand this sutra, and receive, uphold, read, recite, or even transcribe its scrolls and make offerings to them, they will thereby fully accomplish the practice of the six pāramitās.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
How does one believe and resolve upon this sutra, receive and uphold it, read and recite it, and fully practice the six pāramitās?”

The Buddha told Ānanda: "If a son of good family or a daughter of good family has faith and understanding in this sutra, it is called the perfection of giving (dānapāramitā); if they do not give rise to doubt or confusion, it is called the perfection of ethical discipline (śīlapāramitā); if they are capable of enduring this Dharma, it is called the perfection of patience (kṣāntipāramitā); if their minds are free from cowardice or weakness, it is called the perfection of vigor (vīryapāramitā); if their minds are undisturbed and unshaken, it is called the perfection of meditation (dhyānapāramitā); and if they do not engage in conceptual discrimination regarding any phenomena, it is called the perfection of wisdom (prajñāpāramitā)."
Therefore, Ānanda!

This sutra is titled "Corresponding with the Six Pāramitās," and it is also titled "The True Teaching of All Buddhas," and it is also titled "The Vast and Non-regressive Wheel," and it is also titled "The Broad, Sublime, Pure, and Non-regressive Wheel."
"Ānanda! You should receive and uphold these names in this way.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Merely hearing the name of this sutra should lead one to listen to and receive it; how much more so for hearing its exposition in full from beginning to middle to end.
The Buddha told Ānanda:
"So it is, so it is! It is just as you have said.
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If there are those who hear the name of this sutra, how many kalpas of the retribution for birth and death can they eliminate?
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“If there are those who hear the name of the *Vaipulya-viśuddha-avaivartika-cakra-sūtra* and, having heard it,
believe and understand it— Ānanda,
you should know that these sentient beings will eliminate hundreds of thousands of kalpas of birth and death.”
Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
If there are sentient beings who, upon hearing this sutra, are able to believe and understand it and have already resolved to attain bodhicitta, what dharma will they obtain?”
The Buddha told Ānanda:
“Such beings have already received the prediction that they shall attain anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

At that time, each member of the fourfold assembly saw a great lotus flower appear spontaneously before them; the flowers were in full bloom with a hundred or a thousand petals, and possessed hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of radiant colors.
At that time, the fourfold assembly felt immeasurable joy and exultation; they immediately took these flowers and scattered them over the Buddha, saying:
"We vow that in future ages we shall proclaim this sutra just as the World-Honored One does, being exactly equal to him without any difference."
At that time, the World-Honored One smiled.
At that very moment, all musical instruments resounded spontaneously without being struck; all manner of fragrances naturally wafted forth in sweet perfume;
and hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of devas in the void performed great music amidst the sky.
Furthermore, hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of devas, in the midst of the void,
rained down fine powdered sandalwood and various kinds of celestial incense, celestial agallochum incense, and fine powdered tamāla incense;
they also rained down Jambūnada gold dust, silver dust, and celestial maṇi jewels, as well as māndārava flowers.
Mahāmandārava flowers, pāruṣaka flowers, mahāpāruṣaka flowers,
mañjūṣaka flowers, mahāmañjūṣaka flowers, karkarava flowers, mahākarkarava flowers,
rocamāna flowers, mahārocamāna flowers, and śubha flowers.
Mānava flowers, mahāśubhamānava flowers, celestial utpala flowers, kumuda flowers, and puṇḍarīka flowers—
such various flowers as these were scattered over the Buddha.

Various celestial incenses and various celestial garlands, even all the precious jewels belonging to the devas, rained down; the devas in the sky manifested their bodies upon the earth and performed music as an offering to the Buddha, while the people of the world each removed the upper garments they were wearing and scattered them over the Buddha.
Furthermore, there were people who removed their armlets, leglets, necklaces, breast-ornaments, celestial crowns, and flower garlands, scattering them over the Buddha.
Others scattered upon the Buddha golden and silver celestial crowns, celestial crowns of various jewels, celestial crowns of various flowers, and celestial crowns of sandalwood.
Furthermore, there were many people who rejoiced and leaped for joy, their celebration being immeasurable.

At that time, oxen and horses were filled with delight and uttered gentle, harmonious sounds; the various birds in the sky produced melodious and elegant notes; those in the hells and the animal realm were freed from suffering and attained peace; the hungry ghosts were fully satisfied, leaving behind the pains of hunger and thirst; and the devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—all were filled with immeasurable joy and leaped for joy.
At that time, all sentient beings attained a mind of loving-kindness; with minds of loving-kindness directed toward one another, they were free from anger and resentment.
Then Ānanda addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
"For what cause and condition does the World-Honored One smile?
The Buddhas, the Tathāgatas, do not smile without a reason.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:

“Now these four assemblies—monks, nuns, laymen, and laywomen—as well as devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, who have now heard this sutra before me, and those who shall hear this sutra in future ages, shall all never regress from anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi. When they later attain Buddhahood, they shall proclaim this sutra without increase or decrease, exactly as it is today, no different at all.”

When the Buddha preached this sutra, immeasurable, boundless, inconceivable, and limitless hundreds of thousands of millions of billions of nayutas of devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans all became non-retrogressive in their progress toward anuttara-samyak-saṃbodhi.

When the Buddha had finished speaking this sutra, Mañjuśrī the Dharma Prince, boundless and immeasurable bodhisattva-mahāsattvas, the Venerable Ānanda and the great śrāvakas, as well as the fourfold assembly of bhikṣus, bhikṣuṇīs, upāsakas, and upāsikās—[all rejoiced].
The devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and all others in the world, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, were all greatly rejoiced.
The Vaipulya-vaipula-viśuddha-sūtra, Scroll Six.
